## Active

### D-022 — Jump-to-path resolves label paths through Navigator.jumpTo

> _2026-07-09 · realm/blong-commander · active_

The old "Jump to path…" input was a no-op: `onJump` was never wired. The combined crumb/jump
widget's `onJump` now resolves the typed `/`-joined label path through a new
`Navigator.jumpTo(labels)` handle method, which lazy-materializes and reveals the target node.

### D-023 — Commander splitter pane sizes survive reloads

> _2026-07-09 · realm/blong-commander · active_

The splitter state is persisted locally (`stateKey="blong-commander.splitter"`,
`stateStorage="local"`), so pane sizes survive a reload Explorer-style instead of resetting to the
default layout.

### D-024 — Leaf viewers get parent fields by stamping every row

> _2026-08-23 · realm/blong-commander · active_

`commander.node.get` only receives the leaf node, so `{parent.path}` / `{parent.namespace}`
templates could never resolve — the vault viewer 404'd and the S3 bucket came up empty. Changing the
RPC contract to carry the parent was rejected in favour of stamping each row with its direct
parent's fields as `parent.<field>` (`withParentContext`, dropping inherited
`parent.*` to avoid `parent.parent.*` accumulation); `cleanLeafNode` strips those and the `__*`
fields again for viewer display. This stamping is the mechanism every leaf viewer relies on now.

### D-025 — The S3 viewer keeps AWS-native Key instead of lowercasing it

> _2026-08-23 · realm/blong-commander · active_

A first attempt lowercased S3 object list keys (`Key` to `key`) to fit the commander's template
language, which broke the `blong-int-adapter` S3 snapshots and assertions. The adapter was reverted
and the commander source config now uses `keyField: 'Key'` with `{Key}`, plus `{parent.bucket}` from
the stamped context. The rule: prefer fixing the commander config over changing a shared adapter's
wire shape.

### D-026 — Only the top k8s level carries an RBAC permission

> _2026-08-23 · realm/blong-commander · active_

The k8s source's category, resource and item levels used permission strings that were never seeded,
so the gateway's `access.authorization.list` filter dropped them and the tree collapsed to one level
— the namespace became a leaf and opened the wrong viewer. The namespace level's permission now
gates the whole k8s source, and the deeper synthetic levels are ungated.

### D-027 — The commander home is a welcome panel, not a source table

> _2026-08-23 · realm/blong-commander · active_

The initial home tab showed a table of sources that duplicated the tree and was judged useless, so
it was replaced with a `.blong-commander-home` panel: title, hint and clickable source tiles.
`loadRows` with no selection now sets `rows=[]` instead of rendering an unrelated default.

### D-073 — The commander tap test needed the dev intent to provision its DB

> _2026-09-07 · realm/blong-commander · active_

`core/blong-commander/test.ts` loaded with only `['integration']`, so the shared `srv.db` adapter's
`createDatabase`, schema sync and seed — which live under the `dev` intent — never ran and the test
failed with "Unknown database 'commander'". Loading with
`['microservice','integration','dev', ...(CI?['ci']:[])]`, mirroring blong-access, auto-creates the
database, syncs the schema and applies the `meta/db` and `meta/dbTest` seeds.

### D-074 — Commander seed data comes from cluster init jobs

> _2026-09-07 · realm/blong-commander · active_

The backend seeds the commander tests need are provisioned by cluster init jobs in
`test/integration/`, run by `kubectl apply -k test/integration/` in CI and by k3d-create locally, so
no manual step is needed: minio-bucket-init uploads `commander/hello.txt`, a new vault-seed-init
writes the KV-v1 `secret/commander-demo`, a new redis-seed-init sets
`commander:demo`/`commander:greeting`, and kafka-topic-init produces ONE deterministic seed JSON
message. Deterministic content is what makes the CI and local renders identical.

### D-075 — Commander screenshots mask only the dynamic columns

> _2026-09-07 · realm/blong-commander · active_

Whole-table masks were replaced because they are too opaque: the tests now use the Commander's
built-in Filter input to narrow the view to the seeded subset and mask magenta only the genuinely
dynamic columns (vault Accessor, k8s ResourceVersion/Uid/NodeName and pod names, mongo SizeOnDisk,
keycloak realm/user Id and created timestamp, kafka offset), keeping field names and stable columns
visible so a reviewer can tell the UI works. One trap: the filter persists across drill navigation
because it is component-level `search`, so a test must `clearFilter()` before drilling into a child
after a filtered screenshot, or the child view is wrongly filtered — keycloak users came out empty
under the `master` filter, and mongo passed only because its collections carry a `Database=admin`
column.

### D-262 — The redis key shot collapses the node instead of filtering the tree

> _2026-09-24 · realm/blong-commander · active_

The redis-keys explore shot showed the shared dev database own keys in the navigator, written by
every suite that caches anything, so the baseline could never be deterministic. The filter input
narrows the table only: Commander.tsx loads children for the tree through the same loader and then
filters rows, never nodes. The choices were to make the tree follow the filter (a behaviour change
in a shared component, and every suite that filters then drills would re-baseline), to mask the tree
(its height follows the key count, so a mask cannot be stable), or to collapse the drilled node in
the test. I collapsed the node: the path Redis (dev) > 0 stays as evidence that the drill happened,
the table still shows the two seeded keys and the filter that narrowed them, and nothing outside the
test changed. If a filtered navigator is the wanted behaviour, that is a UX decision to take
deliberately rather than through a screenshot.

### D-344 — commanderBranchList orders every level's rows itself

> _2026-10-01 · realm/blong-commander · active_

commanderBranchList now orders a level's rows by the level's labelField, falling back to keyField,
instead of trusting the backend order. Keycloak returns realms unordered, which is why the navigator
could show master and blong-integration in either order and explore-keycloak-users failed in CI
while passing locally. Sorting in the one place every source's children pass through makes the
navigator tree and the table agree and a rerun render the same rows. Accepted consequence: levels
that declare a curated order now come back alphabetical — the k8s category and resource lists are
synthetic and hand-ordered — so explore-k8s-categories, explore-k8s-pods and explore-k8s-pod had
their baselines regenerated with the sorted tree. Ties keep the backend's order (Array#sort is
stable).

### D-481 — The k8s explore shots pin their rows with the filter

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-commander · active_

The commander k8s shots now name the records every cluster carries: `filterRows(page, "kube")` for
the namespace table and `filterRows(page, "coredns")` for the pods table, the idiom the Redis, Vault
and S3 shots already use, because a cluster also lists whatever its own work created (blong-suite,
blong-system) and the unfiltered shot recorded the machine that took it. The two identity columns a
k8s list answer now carries also moved the 1-based `colsMask` positions: namespaces 2,3 to 4,5 and
pods 1,2,4,5,8 to 1,4,6,7,10. Regenerated `explore-k8s-namespaces`, `explore-k8s-pods` and
`explore-k8s-pod` (the viewer reports 22 fields, not 20); `explore-k8s-categories` is synthetic and
unchanged. The navigator still lists the namespaces the taking cluster had, which is inside the 1
percent screenshot tolerance, and is the cue to collapse the source node if a cluster ever carries
many more.

### D-482 — A level filters its rows with declared regexes

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-commander · active_

A commander level may now declare `include` (whitelist) and `exclude` (blacklist) regexes, matched
against the value the level displays (`labelField`, else `keyField`) and applied in
`commanderBranchList` where every source children pass through, beside the ordering that already
lives there. The Kubernetes source needs it: a cluster lists whatever its own work created beside
the four namespaces Kubernetes itself owns, so the navigator tree and the screenshots of it were
reading the cluster instead of the UI. Its namespace level declares
`include: ["^default$", "^kube-"]`. Rejected: a dedicated namespace config key, which would be a
second vocabulary for one concept; and pinning it in the spec, which would pin the test rather than
the product. A deployment still overrides the declaration wholesale through the realm sources
config, which the handler already reads. The selector lives in `branch/` rather than in the
orchestrator group because the framework reports generic code inside a handler group folder as a
load error (observed while running kukum against this realm).

### D-496 — What a commander shot redacts: the value, or the frame around it

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-commander · active_

Which part of a volatile value a commander shot hides, now that masking is gone. A value that varies
whole — a vault accessor, a realm Id, a user Id, a `resourceVersion` — is redacted whole: the
column, its header and the table's shape stay, so a reader can see that the table has an identity
column at all, which a magenta box took with it. A random _number inside a stable frame_ keeps its
frame, which is what `redactCellParts` with `VOLATILE_NUMBER` is for, and the match is the whole
digit run, so the redacted cell is the same width however large the number grows. A created
timestamp is redacted whole rather than digit by digit, and that was the interesting call: its
rendered width depends on the digits it hides (`10/10/2026, 3:03:58 PM` narrows at a single-digit
hour), so hiding digits alone would leave the baseline depending on the values it was hiding. The
pod document viewer is redacted value by value — a quoted string that is not a key, which covers
list items and the escaped JSON some annotations carry — so the field names, the separators and the
line breaks all survive; the bare numbers stay, because a port and a grace period do not vary per
cluster.

## Superseded

### D-479 — The k8s identity columns stale the commander baselines

> _2026-10-10 · realm/blong-commander · superseded_

`withItemIdentity` now puts `apiVersion` and `kind` on every item a k8s list answers, so the
commander explorer, whose columns are the item keys, renders two more columns and its positional
masks (`colsMask`, 1-based) shift. The k8s explore baselines are therefore stale: run 596 failed
`explore-k8s-namespaces.png` with 97724 pixels (7%) different, the baseline showing four columns and
the run six. They have to be regenerated on a cluster shaped like the CI one (k3d created with
`--disable=traefik,servicelb,metrics-server` plus `kubectl apply -k test/integration/`), because the
row sets are the cluster namespace list and its kube-system pods; the running dev-cluster carries
`blong-suite` and `blong-system` from the kustomize work and would bake them in. Decision needed:
recreate a CI-shaped cluster to regenerate there, or leave the regeneration to a run against the CI
cluster.

Superseded by `D-481`.

The shots pin their rows with the filter; both k8s table baselines were regenerated.
